title: Ericsson: 5G must shift focus from consumers to citizens, says UK chief
snippet: The future of 5G in the UK depends on recognising mobile networks as critical national infrastructure and moving beyond the narrow confines of consumer connectivity, according to Nadine Allen, Ericsson's Head of UK. The post Ericsson: 5G must shift focus from consumers to citizens, says UK chief appeared first on Total Telecom.
fullText:
Interview

The future of 5G in the UK depends on recognising mobile networks as critical national infrastructure and moving beyond the narrow confines of consumer connectivity, according to Nadine Allen, Ericsson’s Head of UK.

Speaking at Ericsson’s Elevate 5G event, Allen acknowledged the industry’s 5G revenue gap so far, arguing that 5G SA offers a major opportunity to revitalise 5G through the creation of new commercial models and the integration ofAI.

She called for a shift in perspective, moving away from what consumers want towards what citizens and critical services need.

“We need to shift away from a consumer focus to a citizen focus,” said Nadine. “That means anticipating not what users want from a network, but what they need from a network.”

The UK’s Emergency Services Network (ESN) is a perfect model for this type of collaboration between government and industry, wth Nadine suggesting similar approaches could benefit rail, energy, and defence.

“There are a number of industries that are either in the course of or due to go through quite significant transformation where I think the ESN model or similar can come into play,” said Nadine. “If we look at rail, for example, today on a 2G-based system, they’re moving to the Future Railway Mobile Communication System (FRMCS), which is based on 5G standards. We expect some commercial activity coming up in the foreseeable future for railways.”

The interview also touched on how AI is evolving in the UK and why robust wireless networks will be crucial to its ongoing growth and success.

“We are seeing AI move from data centres to distributed systems. And in order for those things to happen or to be brought to life in a meaningful way, we really have to ensure that we have very solid connectivity and underlying performance in networks,” said Nadine.

Watch the full interview to hear Nadine’s assessment of the UK’s 5G opportunity and what needs to happen next.
